headline: Over 1.27 million students await HSC results to be published Saturday
summary: More than 1.27 million students who sat for the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will receive their results today. Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon will announce the results at 11 AM.
details: Over 1.27 million students who took the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations are set to receive their results today, Saturday. Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon will officially announce the outcomes at 11 AM from the Secondary and Higher Education Division.

Students can access their results through their respective educational institutions, official online portals, or via SMS shortly after the announcement. Preparations for the result publication were finalized on Friday evening, according to Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, chief of the Inter-Board Coordination Committee.

This year, a total of 1,270,583 students participated in the HSC and equivalent examinations, which commenced on July 2 across 2,697 centers nationwide. The average pass rate for the 2024 exams was 77.78 percent, while under the interim government, it stood at 58.83 percent.

Many students are experiencing a mix of anticipation and apprehension, particularly concerning subjects like English. Labait Islam from Gazipur Metropolitan College expressed anxiety about his English results, hoping for a respectable outcome.

Md Limon Islam from Dinajpur's Adarsha College also shared mixed emotions, while Shal Mrong from Nawab Habibullah Model School and College in Dhaka raised concerns about errors in some Physics and Chemistry question papers. Parents are equally anxious about their children's performance.

For those dissatisfied, applications for re-checking answer scripts will be open online from November 1 to November 7. A fee of Tk 150 applies per subject, with separate applications required for two-paper subjects.

Payments for re-scrutiny can be made through various mobile banking services and Sonali Bank. Additionally, students who fail this year's examinations will have the opportunity to retake them within two months of the results' publication.

headline_marked: [[Vegetable prices drop]] by over half in Dhaka markets, bringing relief to buyers
headline: Vegetable prices drop by over half in Dhaka markets, bringing relief to buyers
summary: Dhaka kitchen markets are seeing significant price reductions for most vegetables, with some items dropping by over 50% in the past two weeks, thanks to an increased supply of early-winter produce.
details: Prices of most vegetables have fallen significantly in Dhaka kitchen markets, with some items dropping by more than half over the past two weeks. This relief for buyers is attributed to an increased supply of early-winter produce.

The trend was observed across markets including Shewrapara, Kazipara, Ibrahimpur, Mirpur-1, and Karwan Bazar. Consumers like Ranu Begum noted that early winter vegetables were prohibitively expensive just two weeks prior.

For example, beans that sold for Tk 140-160 per kg two weeks ago were bought for Tk 50 per kg yesterday. Cauliflower and cabbage, previously Tk 60-80 each, are now available for Tk 30-60, and radish dropped from Tk 50 to Tk 25 per kg.

Another shopper, Monjurul Islam, confirmed buying beans for Tk 80 per kg yesterday, down from Tk 120 last week. He also found radish, eggplant, okra, and taro priced reasonably between Tk 40-60 per kg.

Despite these widespread drops, tomatoes and new potatoes remain relatively expensive, still selling for over Tk 150 per kg. A wholesale trader at Karwan Bazar, Sohag Mia, indicated that current supply exceeds demand, making it challenging for traders to profit.
